verdicts.ruling_text: A stochastic candidate must exceed each comparator in each of seeds 0-2, not only in the seed mean; a deterministic candidate is compared with each seed of every stochastic comparator, and its label states that the candidate has no seed variation.

verdicts.evidence: Amendment L170-172 quotes the minimum detectable difference 0.105-0.203 'at alpha = 0.05/8' for H-M3, whose Holm family is 16 (protocol L255-257); microbe_split_lodo_x001_report.json gives 0.112-0.216 at 0.05/16. verdicts.evidence: Amendment L636-648: per-determinand inference is a row bootstrap, which 10.5 itself calls 'optimistic'; the composite is an exact sign-flip test over 7 groups whose smallest two-sided p is 2/2^7 = 0.0156, so it can reject only when all 7 groups agree or nearly so; one group has 14 runs (X). Section 15.1 needs a block bootstrap. A row bootstrap over clustered rows cannot carry a SOTA label.
verdicts.ruling_text: H4 carries no section 15.1 SOTA label: the single pre-declared composite sign-flip test over the 7 EA-test groups is its only confirmatory result, per-determinand results are descriptive and are shown with letter-group cluster intervals, and the row bootstrap is not used for any claim.

verdicts.ruling_text: GEO is scored in `M3/test` and GAS-3 in Test-B only, fixed now; a family that misses a section 7.7 condition is reported descriptively in its own look, and no family changes look after any development number on it exists.

points.point: OQ1 - cap of 10 configuration x track runs, or the strict 8
points.ruling: The cap stays 8. Slot #5 is retired and not reassigned. #6, #7 and #8 run on `lodo` only. The stamp does not approve 10, and the author's fallback (#6 on both tracks) is also refused.
points.reason: Reviewers agree the raise is unapproved; the stricter reading is 3 new runs, not 4. Protocol 10.8 says 8; the 'lead dispatch' for both tracks is not in LEAD_DECISIONS or the handoff; the fallback spends the retired #5 unit. It can be carried out: `lodo` is the primary track, so a lodo-only model can still be M*.

points.point: OQ2 - master vector of 17 dimensions instead of the plan's 14
points.ruling: Accepted as a declared deviation, on condition of full parity: `xgb_v4clr_mo` on all 17 dimensions and `xgb_clr_stack` unconditional on `lodo`. `field_temp_c` is an auxiliary training target only and is never a prediction-time input or a scored target.
points.reason: The extra dimensions were fixed before any fit, so the choice is not post hoc; the risk is that the candidate sees labels its comparators do not (lead rule 3), which the parity condition removes.

points.point: OQ3 - are V4-MR models and +context niche models eligible as M*
points.ruling: `xgb_v4mr` and `xgb_v4mr_stack` are not eligible as M* for H-M3; they are run, reported and used as comparators. NicheInvert-S and NicheGeo-Phys are eligible only under the section 10.4 +context bar, which includes beating `xgb_v4clr_context` and `xgb_nichez_context`.
points.reason: The frozen protocol restricts selection to DNA-encoded candidates with no taxonomy labels (L183, L411-412) and the amendment admits V4-MR is not one. Widening a fixed selection rule after 55 configurations is the less safe option.

points.ruling: Accepted: M*_GEO is selected by the same mechanical rule among the remaining G entries, both models are fixed in one freeze, each claim is scoped to its own family, and every report states that the error rate across the two families can reach 0.10. A GEO result never supports or rescues an H-M3 claim.
points.reason: One model forced on both families would be chosen on 16 targets after the fact; two families with a stated joint error rate is the honest form. Both reviewers accept this with the disclosure.

points.point: OQ5 - which EA rows are scored (designs A, B, C) and the H4 inference
points.ruling: B and C are rejected. If H4 runs: design A, one look on EA-test for H3 and H4, frozen together, EA-dev labels never scored. If H4 does not run: the registered M3E analysis on all 22 groups, unchanged. The choice is made once, in the EA ids freeze, before any EA label file is on disk. H4 has no SOTA label; only the composite test is confirmatory.
points.reason: B scores EA-dev and then trains on it, and C scores EA-test twice; both break campaign rule 1. A is the plan's text and what the lead approved. A cannot let H3 be scored before H4 is frozen, so the amendment's 'H4 never delays M3E/test' is void under A.

points.point: OQ6 - how the M5-X exclusion of ruling 4a is met
points.ruling: H4 stays on hold. After the stamp, the header check decides: with a site key, key-list exclusion plus a counts-only overlap report before the H4 freeze; without one, H4 is not run and is reported as not run, unless the lead re-rules 4a in writing.
points.reason: ENA has dates for all 1,643 grouped runs but no site key. A date-only exclusion is not usable: the M5-X X-U test keys span 2021-2026, so it would remove every row. An exclusion that cannot be shown is not met.

points.point: OQ7 - pinning the Zenodo files and timing of the header check
points.ruling: Accepted: md5 and byte size now, sha256 recorded at download and pinned in the EA freeze, for `water_chem.csv` and for the two ASV files. The header check runs after the stamp, by one hashed script that keeps only the bytes before the first newline in memory and writes nothing else.
points.reason: Zenodo publishes md5 only, so sha256 can exist only after download. The header check is a contact with a label file and is on the amendment's own not-allowed-before-the-stamp list.

points.ruling: Table 1 hyperparameters with a page reference if they can be transcribed; otherwise the full published search space at the published budget. A reduced 60-draw search may be run and reported but is not 'the published method' and cannot be the comparator behind a label.
points.reason: A published comparator re-run with a smaller search is a weakened baseline, which the amendment's own rule ('baselines are never weakened') and section 15.1 forbid.

points.ruling: The lead runs the download through the project downloader after the stamp, with the licence row added first, a size check against the 1 GB cap, and `df` before and after. M3 never reads a key file.
points.reason: Keeps the credential out of the workstream, and puts the 1 GB and 60 GB limits under the lead's eye. GAS-3 is priority 3 and is dropped first if the schedule slips.

points.point: OQ10 - the D1 gate uses the 8 primary targets only
points.ruling: Yes, primary targets only. The gate is evaluated once by the lead after all unconditional comparators, A0 and the diagnostic are finished. The GEO clause is removed from the D2 stop rule, which uses the primary mean alone.
points.reason: The plan words the gate on the 8 targets. Letting any one of 8 GEO point estimates keep D2 alive makes the stop rule easy to escape, so section 12's 'Rule 5 is stricter than the plan' is only partly true.

points.point: OQ11 - a new log file for this amendment
points.ruling: Accepted for execution records only (what ran, when, row ids, counts). Anything that fixes a design choice (D2 hyperparameters, GAS floors, a rerun rule, a spare) needs a stamped deviations file. The stamped amendment and rulings file are set 0444.
points.reason: A log entry is not reviewed and can follow results; the stamp procedure allows changes only in a stamped deviations file before the affected run yields a validation number.

points.point: OQ12 - freeze candidate no later than 2026-11-30
points.ruling: Yes. Arms unfinished on that date are reported as not run and cannot join later; no family is moved to another look for the sake of a label.
points.reason: A fixed date with no late joiners closes the optional-stopping route. It fits the SYNTHESIS schedule (M3 sealed look in the week of Nov 24-30).

missed.issue: The EA kill rules and power were written for design B and cannot be carried over to design A. Under A the scored block is EA-test (549 runs, 7 groups): the rule '< 10 letter groups with >= 10 samples' is then always true, so every determinand is descriptive by construction, and '< 500 linked labelled samples' fails if more than about 9% of rows lack a value.
